The experimental evidence on the impact of BGS exposure on acute mental health has not been sufficiently understood. This scoping review synthesizes 44 experimental studies (2009-2024) to map and characterize the experimental evidence on the acute mental health effects of short-term BGS exposure. METHODS: Following PRISMA-P and the JBI Scoping Review Methodology guidelines, we developed our protocol (https://osf.io/2tvjk/overview) and searched Web of Science, PubMed, Scopus, Embase, PsycINFO, and CNKI for experimental studies. Quality appraisal and risk-of-bias assessment tools were selected according to the study design of each article, and all included studies were evaluated for quality and risk of bias. Evidence was synthesized according to the Population, Exposure, Comparator, Outcome (PECO) framework and then integrated. RESULTS: The existing experimental research was geographically skewed toward Asian cities, and green spaces were more frequently examined than blue spaces. Stress (n = 30), perceived restorativeness (n = 16), and mood (n = 13) were the predominant mental health outcome examined by various physiological and psychological tools. Synthesizing across studies found that brief BGS exposure consistently reduced stress, enhanced mood, and promoted psychological restoration. However, among BGS types and features, more natural settings (e.g., forests, lakesides) outperformed manicured, hardscaped environments, and natural features such as naturalness, plant cover, species richness, and water bodies often amplified benefits. CONCLUSION: This scoping review maps an expanding but methodologically heterogeneous experimental evidence base. Most studies included in our review found that even brief exposure to BGSs, especially those more natural, biodiverse, and water-rich environments, can enhance mental health. Designing and preserving biodiverse, nature-rich, high-quality BGSs is critical for promoting public mental health in rapidly urbanizing contexts. Future experiments should address the paucity of studies on blue spaces, examine multi-sensory effects and the effects of virtual nature, and expand to diverse populations with larger sample sizes.

title: Environmentally relevant antibiotic exposure in school-age children: unraveling socio-dietary drivers in a multi-ethnic region of Northwest China
abstract: While existing biomonitoring studies have extensively characterized the prevalence of antibiotic exposure, the complex sociodemographic and behavioral determinants underlying individual exposure profiles remain insufficiently understood. This study addressed the important research gap by examining antibiotic exposure in a distinctive socio-cultural setting-the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region of China. We analyzed urinary concentrations of 22 antibiotics from four classes (tetracyclines, sulfonamides, macrolides, and fluoroquinolones) and one additional synthetic antibacterial agent in a cohort of 295 children in 2024. A brief food-frequency survey was concurrently administered to evaluate the nutritional preferences of children. The results revealed extensive exposure to antimicrobial agents, with 55.4% of the participants exhibiting measurable traces of at least one target antimicrobial compound. Detection frequencies for individual compounds ranged from 0.7% to 26.4%. Multivariable logistic regression analyses revealed that specific dietary habits were associated with increased odds of antibiotic detection; notably, after false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment, frequent consumption of white meat and eggs was significantly associated with higher detection odds for tetracyclines (OR = 2.54) and fluoroquinolones (OR = 2.96), respectively. Health risk assessment based on the hazard index (HI) and hazard quotient indicated that 9.15% of the children had HI values exceeding 1. Ciprofloxacin was the primary contributor to HI, with hazard quotient values exceeding 1 detected in 2.71% of children. Overall, this biomonitoring study indicates frequent internal exposure to environmentally relevant antibiotics among school-age children in this region, underscoring the need for further multi-pathway exposure assessments.

title: Prenatal exposure to di(isononyl) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate and adverse birth outcomes in the USA: a prospective analysis of births in a large American birth cohort
abstract: BACKGROUND: A large body of evidence has documented the effects of ortho-phthalates, additives to soft plastic used in food packaging, on premature birth. Ortho-phthalates are increasingly replaced with alternatives including tere-phthalates and di(isononyl) cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate (DINCH). A limited toxicological literature suggests that DINCH metabolites disrupt sex hormones and promote oxidant stress known to contribute to adverse birth outcomes, and epidemiologic studies have also been limited in sample size, inclusivity of different populations and measurements at different time points in pregnancy. METHODS: We leveraged a large American cohort comprised of mother-child dyads from twenty-two cohorts to assess associations of trimester-specific and pregnancy-wide DINCH metabolites with birth weight (BW) and gestational age (GA). FINDINGS: Average prenatal urinary DINCH was inversely associated with birth length, birthweight, and birthweight for gestational age z-scores, but not GA. A tenfold increase in the pregnancy-averaged DINCH metabolite cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylic acid-monocarboxy isooctyl ester (MCOCH) was associated with a decrease of 27.43 g (95%CI: -54.81, -0.04) in birthweight. Trimester-specific analyses revealed stronger associations for third trimester DINCH exposure with birth outcomes. INTERPRETATION: In a large American cohort representing a broad range of backgrounds, we identified an inverse association of DINCH with standardized measures of birth size, but not gestational age. Further studies should examine joint exposures to DINCH, tere- and orthophthalates, and repeated measures across pregnancy.

title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics reveals chronic GenX exposure-induced neurotoxicity and predicted alterations in microglia-neuron communication networks in mouse brain
abstract: GenX (hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid, HFPO-DA), an emerging replacement for legacy per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), has raised increasing concerns regarding its potential health risks. However, the neurotoxic effects and underlying mechanisms of chronic GenX exposure remain poorly understood. In the present study, we established a chronic oral gavage mouse model of GenX exposure and combined targeted UPLC-MS/MS analysis, molecular biological validation, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) to systematically investigate GenX exposure-induced significant motor and memory deficits in mice. Targeted UPLC-MS/MS analysis revealed accumulation of GenX in blood, liver, and brain tissues. In addition, GenX exposure disrupted both the intestinal barrier and blood-brain barrier, as evidenced by increased Evans blue extravasation and reduced expression of tight junction proteins. snRNA-seq analysis revealed broad transcriptional alterations across multiple brain cell populations. Neuronal populations exhibited enrichment of neurodegeneration- and apoptosis-related pathways, and abnormal expression of apoptosis-associated proteins. Moreover, microglia displayed inflammatory activation characterized by increased expression of activation-related genes, activation of NLRP3/Caspase-1 signaling, and altered pseudotime trajectories marked by decreased P2ry12 and increased Apoe expression. CellChat analysis further predicted alterations in microglia-neuron communication networks involving NRXN, NCAM, Cx3cl1-Cx3cr1, and Gas6-Mertk signaling pathways. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that chronic GenX exposure induces broad neurotoxic alterations involving barrier dysfunction, neuronal apoptosis, microglial inflammatory activation, and disrupted intercellular communication, providing new insights into the neurotoxic mechanisms of emerging PFAS substitutes.

title: Sub‑chronic PFOA exposure at human‑relevant increasing doses in male mice: Role of stress‑induced gut barrier disruption in shaping intestinal and hepatic responses under high-dose conditions
abstract: In humans, dietary intake is thought to be the main route of exposure to perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). The gastrointestinal tract is the primary entry point for this highly persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutant; however, its fate and effects within the digestive system remain largely unknown. Combining biology-based approaches with mass-spectrometry chemical imaging, our study investigated the impact of 90-day oral exposure to PFOA at a dose relevant to highly exposed human populations on an intact versus stress-impaired gut barrier in adult male mice. A ten-day corticosterone treatment was used to develop an intestinal hyperpermeability model. Unlike this model, exposure to PFOA at 15,000 ng/kg body weight/day did not impair gut barrier integrity nor gut microbiota composition or metabolic functions, when considered separately. However, integrating the 16S metabarcoding and metabolomic datasets revealed subtle yet significant effects of PFOA exposure including a decrease in Lactobacillus, Orodobacter and Ligilactobacillus, as well as changes in short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate) and cholic acid. The impact on the liver was determined by simultaneously assessing functional enzymatic activity and mRNA expression of xenobiotic metabolising enzymes. Notably, CYP2C37 activity was inhibited by PFOA exposure under both control and corticosterone conditions. Hepatic homeostasis was also assessed, revealing changes at the transcriptional level in cholesterol transport and biosynthesis pathways, though with no major downstream functional effects. PFOA was found to accumulate in the hepatocyte cytosol as well as in intestinal goblet cells. This work, conducted at human-relevant doses, paves the way for future health risk assessments of PFOA and other substances belonging to the extremely large PFAS family.

title: Nano-selenium suppresses cuproptosis to restore mitophagic flux and alleviate deoxynivalenol-induced renal inflammation
abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a widespread mycotoxin contaminating cereal grains and animal feed, posing significant risks to livestock health and food safety. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying DON-induced nephrotoxicity remain poorly understood. In this study, we identify cuproptosis as a critical driver of DON-induced nephrotoxicity in chickens and investigate the protective role of nano-selenium (Nano-Se). DON exposure disrupted copper homeostasis and induced cuproptosis, as evidenced by dysregulation of FDX1, LIAS, and DLAT, resulting in mitochondrial oxidative damage and electron transport chain (ETC) dysfunction. Excessive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) further impaired lysosomal acidification, resulting in lysosomal membrane permeabilization (LMP) and blockade of mitophagic flux, ultimately triggering a robust inflammatory response. Nano-Se supplementation effectively mitigated DON-induced renal injury by suppressing cuproptosis, restoring mitochondrial redox balance, preserving ETC function, rescuing lysosomal function, re-establishing mitophagic flux, and attenuating inflammatory responses in vivo and in vitro. Mechanistically, pharmacological modulation targeting copper levels, mtROS generation, or mitophagic flux abolished the protective effects of Nano-Se. Collectively, these findings reveal that DON induces nephrotoxicity via the cuproptosis-mtROS-mitophagy axis and that Nano-Se ameliorates DON-induced renal inflammation by suppressing cuproptosis, reducing mtROS accumulation, and restoring mitophagic flux. This study provides a mechanistic basis for the use of Nano-Se as a potential therapeutic agent against mycotoxin-associated renal injury, with implications for environmental health risk assessment and livestock production.

title: Inadequate waste management drives the spread of antimicrobial resistance across the watershed of a large African city
abstract: Rapid urbanization in the Global South consistently outpaces sanitation infrastructure, transforming urban rivers into AMR reservoirs. Yet watershed-scale quantification of resistomes in such settings remains scarce, limiting exposure risk assessment and intervention planning. Here we present the most detailed spatial baseline for waterborne AMR in sub-Saharan Africa, using the Akaki River (Addis Ababa, Ethiopia) as a model system for rapidly urbanizing megacity watersheds with inadequate sanitation. We sampled 38 sites across an extreme pollution gradient during the dry season, when low flow produces maximum pollutant concentrations and the highest resident exposure risk. Water quality, microbiome marker data, 309 antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and 57 mobile genetic elements (MGEs) were quantified by high-throughput quantitative PCR. ARG and MGE abundances in central urban reaches exceeded 10 1 ⁰ gene copies L⁻ 1 , indistinguishable from untreated sewage. Critically, clinically important ARGs co-occurred widely with broad-host-range MGEs, including the IncP-1α plasmid backbone, IS 26 , IS Ecp1 , IS 6100 , and class 1 integron integrase genes, indicating that ARGs are primed for potential horizontal gene transfer in waters where hundreds of thousands of Addis residents bathe, wash, and irrigate food crops. Dissolved oxygen depletion and elevated NH 4 -N correlated significantly with resistome expansion ( p < 0.01), serving as robust chemical proxies for diffuse, system-wide raw sewage inputs that carry the actual mechanistic AMR drivers (e.g., heavy metals, antibiotic residues, and resistant hosts). The 38-site spatial design and dry-season worst-case conditions together provide a replicable model for AMR exposure assessment in comparable Global South cities.

title: Reduced regulatory testing of biochemical plant protection products: an evaluation using three case studies
abstract: Biochemicals are increasingly used in plant protection strategies due to their generally favorable safety profiles and rapid environmental degradation and are currently subject to the same extensive data requirements as conventional synthetic chemicals in Europe. The BiochemPPP-STAS framework was developed to consider these differences and to provide a concept for reduced and triggered information requirements. Here, we report on three case studies to compare the outcome of the BiochemPPP-STAS concept with the traditional information requirements for regulatory human health and environmental risk assessment. Three biochemicals, gibberellic acid (GA3), Lysate of Willaertia magna C2c Maky lysate (LWm) and tea tree oil (TTO) were retrospectively assessed using regulatory authority evaluations. For all three case studies, BiochemPPP-STAS adequately identified hazard profiles and supported derivation of reference values comparable to those obtained using full conventional data packages, while substantially reducing resources and in particular animal testing. For GA3 and LWm, the base dataset was sufficient to characterize toxicity and support low-risk conclusions. For TTO, reproductive toxicity signals were identified in base studies and triggered higher-tier testing, demonstrating the responsiveness of the tiered approach. Quantitative differences in reference values compared with classical assessments were generally small and did not alter regulatory outcomes. Environmental assessments similarly showed that base data requirements captured ecotoxicological concerns. The assessments on environmental safety were not different than using the full data set. Although conclusions are limited by the small number of case studies, and additional evaluations are necessary, the findings support, as a proof of concept the scientific adequacy of the BiochemPPP-STAS.

title: Corrigendum to “Sparse group lasso weighted quantile sum regression for analyzing chemical mixture effects: bidirectional effect estimation with two-stage group-level evaluation” [Environ. Int. 215 (2026) 110480]
Toward NGRA for safer phthalate substitution: An AOP-informed IATA case study integrating AI-based predictions and in vitro NAM evidence for DART prioritization
abstract: Plasticizer substitution can address concerns about regulated legacy phthalates, but decisions based on incomplete hazard and exposure evidence may result in regrettable substitution. We evaluated whether an adverse outcome pathway (AOP)-informed framework integrating predictions from ToxBAI, an AI-based toxicity prediction platform, with experimental new approach methodologies (NAMs) evidence could support screening-level prioritization of plasticizers for male reproductive developmental toxicity within the broader domain of developmental and reproductive toxicity (DART). Four legacy phthalates and four alternative plasticizers were assessed using regulatory data, literature-derived in vitro evidence, ToxCast bioactivity data, ToxBAI toxicity predictions, in vitro-to-in vivo extrapolation-derived human-equivalent doses (HEDs), and exposure records from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database. Evidence was mapped onto an AOP network involving steroidogenesis, androgen signaling, and male reproductive tract malformations. Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate and dibutyl phthalate showed coherent evidence across regulatory outcomes, AOP-linked key events, and HED-scaled bioactivity, supporting high concern for DART. Diethyl phthalate and di-n-octyl phthalate showed less consistent mechanistic support. Alternative plasticizers generally exhibited fewer active signals, but this pattern should be interpreted given limited assay coverage and sparse concentration-response data for DART-related mechanisms. Internal exposure evidence for sensitive developmental and reproductive windows was sparse. Isolated signals involving PPARα activation, testosterone-related responses, and androgen receptor activity indicated that these alternatives cannot yet be confirmed as safer substitutes. Overall, AOP-informed integration of ToxBAI predictions with existing NAMs, regulatory, and exposure evidence provided a transparent screening-level prioritization framework and identified uncertainties relevant to safer substitution. This hazard-focused IATA case study provides a mechanistic foundation for future exposure-informed NGRA.

title: Benzo[a]pyrene and bisphenol A interact to induce combined pulmonary toxicity through an integrated transcriptomic-metabolomic network
abstract: Widespread atmospheric pollutants such as benzo[a]pyrene (BaP) and bisphenol A (BPA) persistently coexist, yet their combined risks to the respiratory system remain largely overlooked. In this study, C57BL/6J mouse and A549 cell models were employed to investigate the combined pulmonary toxicity induced by BaP and BPA, with an integrated transcriptomic-metabolomic framework established to characterize their response patterns. Combined exposure to BaP and BPA caused pathological damage in mouse lung tissue and specifically induced a broader spectrum of adverse effects. In vitro experiments demonstrated that combined exposure induced cytotoxicity, including FOXM1-mediated changes in cell survival and EGFR/AKT pathway-mediated alterations in the invasive phenotype. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses indicated that combined exposure suppressed immune cell populations, especially CD8 T cells, and disrupted glycerophospholipid metabolism. We further categorized these outcomes into four interaction response patterns, which may facilitate the more precise identification of target information within specific interaction contexts. In addition, glycerophosphocholine (GPC) was found to mediate the overall immunosuppressive effects caused by combined exposure, while had a limited effect on changes in lung cell populations. We suggest that greater attention be paid to the interaction characteristics between mixed pollutants and their molecular targets within the framework of joint health risk assessment, to improve the mechanistic understanding of complex combined toxic effects.

title: Single-Cell Metallomics of ovarian granulosa cells enables assessment of Low-Level heavy metal exposure associated with impaired human oocyte development
abstract: The oocyte microenvironment, comprising ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) and follicular fluid (FF), sustains oocyte development with nutrients and regulatory signals but may also transfer heavy metals to the oocyte. While high concentrations of heavy metals in FF and blood have been associated with impaired oocyte development, the effect of low-level exposure on the oocyte remains unclear, partly due to the analytical challenges in measuring low-level heavy metals in biological fluids. Here, we investigated the associations between low-level heavy metal exposure and oocyte development. Using a highly sensitive single-cell metallomic technique, we analyzed ovarian GCs collected from women undergoing in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer (IVF-ET) to serve as a biomarker of intracellular heavy metal burden in the peri-oocyte microenvironment. The associations between heavy metals in GCs and reproductive outcomes across multiple key reproductive stages were analyzed. Our results showed that the heavy metals content in GCs were generally below 0.5 fg/cell. Higher mean intensities and prevalence of several metals in GCs were significantly associated with reduced oocyte maturation rate, normal fertilization rate, and good-quality embryo rate (all adjusted P < 0.05). Elevated intracellular levels of lead and mercury were also associated with adverse reproductive outcomes and increased risk of early miscarriage. In contrast, higher heterogeneity of Hg within GCs was associated with reduced miscarriage risk (OR = 0.37 [0.04, 0.92], P = 0.034). Notably, these associations are significantly contributed by intercellular heterogeneity of metal accumulation within the GC population. Our study demonstrates the feasibility of applying single-cell metallomic technique to ovarian GCs to assess the reproductive risk associated with low-level intracellular heavy metal burden in ovarian follicles, and underscores the need for further reducing environmental heavy metal exposure to protect female reproductive health.

title: Mortality during heatwaves in Spain, 2015–2025: heat metrics, patterns and future risks
abstract: The summer of 2025 was exceptionally warm in Spain, ranking among the most extreme heat seasons on record and highlighting the need to better understand its health impacts. We analyzed the relationship between heat and mortality across the 2015-2024 period, using Spain's high-resolution mortality surveillance and meteorological data. We evaluated multiple heat metrics at different spatial scales to identify those most strongly associated with mortality during heatwaves. We found that event-level heat metrics can explain a large proportion of the variability in heatwave mortality, with extreme temperature and cumulative exposure providing the best performance. In particular, heat-attributable mortality increased by 15 % (95 % CI: 6.7-24.3 %) nationwide and by 24 % (95 % CI: 15.3-33.4 %) at the provincial level for each 1 °C increase in average daily maximum temperature during a heatwave. Over the study period, heat-attributable deaths declined annually by 3.9-5.8 % after adjusting for temperature, yet forecasts substantially overestimated the exceptional heatwaves of 2025. When combined with climate projections, results indicate increased risks in inland regions where warming and vulnerability converge. Spain's experience offers valuable lessons for other regions facing increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves.

title: Identification of priority gaseous component in biodiesel exhaust and its potential pulmonary hazards: a data-driven screening and validation strategy
abstract: Biodiesel is increasingly adopted as a renewable low-carbon fuel, yet the pulmonary toxicity of its exhaust-particularly the gaseous components-remains a critical knowledge gap. To address this, we developed an integrative strategy combining data-driven prioritization with experimental validation. Herein, we employ a multidimensional risk-ranking system that predicts pulmonary fibrosis as the top-ranked adverse outcome (weighted score: 1.00) and ranks formaldehyde as the highest-priority toxicant (weighted score: 0.94). Component-outcome association analysis further predicts aldehydes, particularly formaldehyde, as the top candidate driving pulmonary fibrosis, with an estimated 28% contribution. Both in vivo and in vitro validations demonstrate that biodiesel exhaust (BDE) gas exposure induces substantial pulmonary fibrogenic toxicity, with formaldehyde directly driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in lung epithelial cells. By integrating quantitative proteomics with computational network toxicology, we identify TGF-β1 as a key mediator linking formaldehyde to fibrotic remodeling. This conclusion is further suppported by the upregulation of Tgfb1 expression both in vivo and in vitro. Moreover, analysis of a human Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) single-cell dataset highlighted immature neutrophils as a candidate immune subset enriched for the formaldehyde-pulmonary fibrosis-associated gene signature. Overall, this study systematizes the pulmonary toxicity profile of BDE gaseous components and provides an evidence-based foundation for incorporating BDE-derived aldehydes, specifically formaldehyde, into health risk assessments and future emission control policies for biodiesel.

title: Regional heterogeneity in heat mortality reduction by urban cooling strategies across Chinese cities
abstract: Driven by climate change, extreme heat events pose growing health threats across China. Although infrastructure-based urban cooling strategies have been promoted, the regional disparities in their cooling efficacy and health benefits remain insufficiently quantified. Using the WRF-SLUCM and regional temperature-mortality exposure-response relationships, this study simulated four typical cooling measures (Green Roof, Cool Roof, Street Tree, and Full Adaptation) across 319 Chinese cities during summer 2022 and quantified heat-related mortality reductions. Results show that Full Adaptation reduces heat mortality by 18.8 % (95 % CI: 12.7 %-24.5 %), while Cool Roof, Green Roof, and Street Tree achieve 11.2 % (95 % CI: 7.6 %-14.6 %), 11.0 % (95 % CI: 7.4 %-14.3 %) and 5.5 % (95 % CI: 3.3 %-7.5 %) reductions, respectively. Beyond regional differences in cooling efficacy, variation in dRR/dT is another key determinant of overall effectiveness. This study emphasizes that the deployment of infrastructure‑based strategies at the regional level should balance both efficiency and equity principles. East China, with its large exposed urban population, delivers the greatest total health benefits. Regions with higher temperature sensitivity, such as Southwest and Northwest China, achieve larger per‑capita mortality reductions per unit temperature drop. In regions such as South China, where populations have developed substantial heat acclimatization, the mortality mitigation effect of cooling interventions is comparatively limited. These findings confirm the effectiveness of infrastructure‑based urban cooling strategies in reducing heat‑related mortality risk across China, while also revealing substantial regional heterogeneity, suggesting that priority should be balanced between areas of high temperature sensitivity and those with large population exposure.

title: Corrigendum to “Association between blood lipid levels in early pregnancy and urinary organophosphate metabolites in the Japan Environment and Children’s Study” [Environ. Int. 190 (2024) 108932]
Health and economic benefits of air quality improvements in France through diverse net-zero transition scenarios by 2050
abstract: Abstract Background Climate mitigation policies just with air quality improvements can deliver substantial co-benefits through reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and air pollutant concentrations. Mitigation strategies range from sufficiency to technology-driven transitions, yet linked co-benefits remain poorly understood. This study evaluates PM 2.5 and NO 2 exposure changes and associated co-benefits using France’s energy-transition scenarios. Methods Emission projections were incorporated to the CHIMERE chemistry-transport model to estimate PM 2.5 and NO 2 concentrations for 2030 and 2050. Health impacts were assessed using disease-specific cessation-lag assumptions relative to 2019, covering premature mortality, morbidity, DALYs, and economic benefits across nine outcomes (hypertension, lung cancer, ischaemic heart disease, stroke, COPD, type-2 diabetes, acute lower respiratory infections, and asthma in children and adults). Findings Population exposure in continental France is projected to decline by 23% and 45% for PM 2.5 and NO 2 by 2030, rising to 40% and 70% by 2050. Health gains are substantial and broadly consistent across all four scenarios, with modest differences between sufficiency-oriented and technology-driven pathways. Under delayed-impact assumptions, which accounts for the latency between exposure reduction and health response, avoided premature deaths reached 8,800-9,300 for PM 2.5 and 11,000-12,800 for NO 2 in 2030, rising to 21,300-22,100 and 24,500-26,200 by 2050. Avoided morbidity cases grew from 51,100–55,200 in 2030 to 84,000-87,800 by 2050, with total DALYs averted increasing from 278,000-310,000 to 427,000-450,000 over the same period. Economic benefits scaled accordingly, direct medical cost savings reached €1.0-1.1 billion/year by 2050, with intangible cost savings of €41-43 billion with PM 2.5 and €36-39 billion with NO 2 reductions. Conclusion Net-zero transition delivers substantial, progressive health and economic co-benefits that are robust across diverse policy pathways. Rather than sectoral composition, commitment to decarbonisation itself drives air quality improvements and population health gains. These findings support integrating co-benefits into climate policy frameworks to strengthen the evidence base for ambitious mitigation action. Highlights Net-zero policies can deliver large air-quality co-benefits; here, chemistry-transport modeling coupled with emission projections quantifies these benefits across four contrasting French decarbonisation pathways for 2030 and 2050. Health and economic co-benefits are large and robust across all four contrasting scenarios, with modest differences between sufficiency-oriented and technology-driven pathways. By 2050, PM 2.5 and NO 2 concentrations decline by 38-40% and 70-75%, averting 20,000-22,000 and 24,500-26,200 attributable premature deaths annually. Avoided morbidity reaches 84,000-87,800 cases/year and DALYs averted reach 427,000-450,000/year in 2050, growing substantially from 2030 estimates. Monetization of health impacts results in, direct medical savings of €1 billion/year in 2050 and intangible cost savings of €43 billion (PM 2.5 ) and €38 billion (NO 2 ) per year.

title: Beyond targeted PFAS: contamination patterns and trophic dynamics in an estuarine food web
abstract: Over the past decade, emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have been increasingly reported in aquatic environments. Still, the environmental behavior of numerous emerging PFAS remains poorly understood. This study investigated trophic dynamics and contamination patterns of both legacy and emerging PFAS revealed by HRMS, in the food web of common sole (benthic) and European sea bass (demersal). Overall, 14 estuarine species collected in the Seine Estuary (France) were studied, including zooplankton, polychaetes, shellfish, crustaceans and fish. Through suspect screening, 92 PFAS belonging to 31 classes were detected, several of which were found in all samples (e.g., FHxSA and 6:2 FTSAm), and further (semi-)quantified using an innovative similarity-based approach. 6:2 FTAB was identified as one of the most abundant compounds in all samples, with concentrations up to five times higher (62 ng/g wet weight (ww)) than the highest PFOS concentration (12 ng/g ww). Contamination profiles appeared to be influenced by habitat, trophic level and metabolic capacities. An influence of habitat was evidenced, with benthic organisms being mainly contaminated by long-head precursors (e.g., X:2 FTAB and X:2 FTSA-HOPrS), and pelagic organisms primarily by short-head precursors (FASA and X:3 FTCA), PFCA and PFSA. Across the food web, concentrations of long-head precursors tended to decrease with trophic level, while concentrations of short-head precursors, PFCA and PFSA tended to increase, suggesting a biotransformation of long-head precursors in the organisms of higher trophic levels. Finally, fish species showed relatively lower levels of long-head precursors, strengthening the hypothesis of biotransformation processes by the liver.

title: Gestational exposure to hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid impairs the reproductive function of male offspring through the LCN2-ferroptosis axis in spermatocytes
abstract: Hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA), introduced as an industrial replacement for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), has raised concern regarding its potential bioaccumulation and toxicity. However, the reproductive toxicity and mechanistic basis of HFPO-TA prenatal exposure in male offspring remain unclear. A mouse model of gestational HFPO-TA exposure (0.4 and 1 mg/kg/day) was established, and integrated histopathological assessment, single-cell transcriptomics, and molecular simulation approaches were performed to characterize its effects on male offspring. HFPO-TA exposure significantly impaired the reproductive function in F1 male mice, as indicated by reduced testicular weight and sex hormone levels, compromised sperm quality, spermatocyte meiotic arrest, and increased germ cell apoptosis. Single-cell sequencing revealed that prenatal HFPO-TA exposure triggered ferroptosis in spermatocytes of male offspring mice and identified lipocalin-2 (Lcn2) as a key regulator of this response. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations confirmed stable binding between HFPO-TA and LCN2. In vitro experiments further demonstrated that HFPO-TA induced spermatocyte ferroptosis through lipid peroxidation and iron overload, while these effects were reversed by treatment with the ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 or by Lcn2 overexpression. Collectively, this study delineated a mechanistic framework in which prenatal HFPO-TA exposure induces spermatocyte-specific injury of male offspring through the LCN2-ferroptosis pathway, providing a scientific basis for health risk assessment and regulation in the use of next-generation per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances.

title: Sputum microplastic concentrations and their association with underweight in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: first human evidence combined with integrated network toxicology analysis
abstract: Weight loss is a prevalent symptom in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Nevertheless, the role of microplastics (MPs) in this process remains poorly understood, and the underlying mechanisms are still unknown. We measured 13 MPs types by pyrolysis–gas chromatography-mass spectrometry in sputum from 40 COPD patients. Body composition was assessed using bioelectrical impedance analysis. A hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis explored the potential molecular mechanisms linking MPs exposure to alterations of body composition in COPD. Of the 40 participants, 12 (30.0%) were classified as underweight. Disease stage, nutritional status, and inflammatory indicators did not differ significantly between the two groups. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) was detected in 97.5% of samples and showed the highest median concentration. PVC and total MPs showed non-linear positive associations with the odds of underweight in COPD, with fully adjusted odds ratios of 4.324 and 4.497. Sensitivity analyses also acquired the similar results. Higher PVC and total MPs were associated with reduced fat mass ( P < 0.05), and linear regression models adjusted for all covariables showed similar negative associations. Exploratory mediation analysis showed that after adjustment for fat mass, the negative association between PVC exposure and body mass index (BMI) was no longer observed, suggesting that this association may be explained by reduced fat mass. Using the low-molecular-weight constituents of PVC and its additives (vinyl chloride monomer and phthalates) as the exposure sources, hypothesis-generating network toxicology analysis identified 84 targets shared with COPD and weight loss, enriched in inflammatory and adipocyte-differentiation signaling (adjusted P = 8.4 × 10⁻ 15 and 2.1 × 10⁻ 10 ). In conclusion, sputum MPs exposure was associated with higher odds of underweight and with lower fat mass in COPD patients. Chemicals-driven inflammatory signaling and impaired adipocyte differentiation may be involved in MPs-associated weight loss in COPD, which needs to be verified by experimental evidences.

title: Air pollution and bone fractures in a high-risk population: differences by age and sex
abstract: Purpose Fracture incidence is high in Norway compared to other European countries. We examined whether ambient air pollution levels are associated with forearm and hip fracture incidence, and whether these associations differed by sex and age. Methods Register data on 127,799 forearm fractures (age ≥40 years) and 103,754 hip fractures (age ≥50 years) were linked to population data from Statistics Norway (2008–2018). Annual levels of particulate matter <2.5 µm (PM 2.5 ) and nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ) were modelled in the NordicWelfAir project using the Urban Background Model and combined via ArcGIS. Fracture Incidence Rate Ratios (IRRs) with 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) by pollutant levels were estimated using Poisson regression, adjusting for education level, marital status, and immigrant background, urban/rural and inland location, health region, and climate, and examining interactions by sex and age (multiplicative and additive). Results PM 2.5 ranged from 0.90–66.1 µg/m 3 (mean: 5.5) and NO 2 from 0.20–72.2 µg/m 3 (mean: 8.1). In the highest PM 2.5 tertile compared to the lowest, age- and year-adjusted forearm fracture risk was IRR = 1.22 (95% CI: 1.18, 1.25) in men and IRR = 1.24 (95% CI: 1.22, 1.26) in women. They were partly attenuated after adjusting for annual temperature and geographic variables. Associations with NO 2 and with hip fractures were similar, though weaker. Interactions by sex and age were present for both fracture types, most notably a stronger NO 2 – hip fracture association in individuals aged ≥80 years. Conclusion Ambient air pollution is associated with fracture risk, even at low exposure levels. The most consistent finding was a stronger association among individuals aged 80 years and above.

title: Prenatal exposure to PFAS and multimodal structural brain development across childhood
abstract: BACKGROUND: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are ubiquitous environmental pollutants that are posited to be neurotoxic to the developing brain; however, the impact of prenatal exposure to PFAS - particularly to newer, short-chain PFAS - on brain development across childhood is unclear. METHODS: Concentrations of 9 PFAS were quantified in cord blood plasma of 452 infants (440 for the diffusion sample) who later participated in structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) at ages 4.5, 6, 7.5, and 10.5 years, providing estimates of regional cortical thickness and surface area, subcortical volumes, and fractional anisotropy (FA) of key white matter tracts. Longitudinal mixed-effect models estimated associations of PFAS with age 4.5 brain metrics and their developmental trajectories across childhood after correcting for the false discovery rate within PFAS and outcome domains. RESULTS: Higher concentrations of PFNA and PFDA in cord blood were associated with lower model-estimated age 4.5 surface area of the right paracentral lobule. PFHpA was associated with faster surface area growth in the left rostral anterior cingulate and slower growth in the right caudal middle frontal gyrus from 4.5 to 10.5 years. The short-chain compound PFBS was linked with greater model-estimated age 4.5 FA in 12 white matter tracts, while PFOA and PFNA were linked with lower FA in the middle cerebellar peduncle and the left corticospinal tract, respectively. Associations of PFBS with FA attenuated with age in several tracts. CONCLUSIONS: Prenatal exposure to PFAS was associated with altered development of frontal and paracentral regions and of white matter microstructure. These findings highlight the need for further research examining the long-term associations of prenatal exposure to PFAS with children's neurodevelopment.

title: A framework for assessing human internal microplastic exposure through dataset alignment and quality screening
abstract: Determining human microplastic exposure from external intake estimates combined with biodistribution modelling remains highly uncertain because errors propagate across multiple pathways and assumptions. We therefore present a framework for estimating internal human microplastic exposure directly from published measurements in organs, tissues, and bodily fluids. The framework integrates dataset selection, QA/QC screening, and an updated mathematical alignment method incorporating statistical fitting, goodness-of-fit testing, and comparison of alternative particle-size distributions to support cross-compartment comparison and whole-body inference. As a proof of principle, we applied this approach to published human microplastic particle data under two scenarios: an 'as measured' scenario and a 'biologically plausible' scenario in which particle size distributions were truncated at literature-based accessibility limits. The scenarios produced strongly divergent mean estimates: 159.4 mg (80.9-824; parametric 95 % Monte Carlo interval) under the 'as measured' scenario and 0.41 mg (0.22-1.56; parametric 95 % Monte Carlo interval) for the truncated 'biologically plausible' scenario. This 388-fold divergence shows that current quantitative inference is dominated by assumptions about the treatment of unusually large particles and data quality. The values should therefore be interpreted as scenario-bounded framework outputs conditional on the currently available, clinically biased dataset, and not as estimates representative of healthy populations or the general population. The framework also yielded apparent, size-dependent organ-to-blood ratios that may serve as provisional benchmarks or hypothesis-generating boundary conditions for future physiologically based kinetic (PBK) model development, but not yet as validated tissue-partitioning constants. Although current data quality limits regulatory-grade quantification, the framework provides a transparent basis for exposure assessment using human monitoring data, for identifying key uncertainties, and for illustrating potential future regulatory application.

title: Detection of the PFAS ADV in a non-occupationally exposed population living in Northern Italy
abstract: BACKGROUND: ADVs are substances derived from polymerized perfluoropolyether carboxylic acids (Cl-PFPECAs), produced exclusively at a fluoropolymer plant in Northern Italy. Available evidence on human exposure to ADV is limited, particularly in populations without occupational exposure and living outside the immediate vicinity of the manufacturing source. This study aimed to characterize serum ADV concentrations in a non-occupationally exposed population living in Northern Italy. METHODS: A total of 150 non-occupationally exposed individuals residing and/or working in Pavia, Northern Italy, were enrolled from the IDEA study (2024-2026). Participants underwent clinical evaluation and blood sampling, and serum concentrations of six ADV isomers were measured using a validated UHPLC-MS/MS method. Associations of ADV-N2 concentrations with demographic, biochemical, and hematological parameters were investigated using multivariable regression models. RESULTS: ADV-N2 showed the highest detection frequency (98.0% of samples above the LOD), followed by ADV-N3 and ADV-M3, whereas the other isomers were detected rarely or not detected. ADV-N2 concentrations were higher in men than in women. An age × sex interaction analysis indicated different age-related patterns of ADV-N2 concentrations in women and men, with a stronger positive age-related estimate among women. Exploratory analyses of biochemical and hematological parameters showed positive association estimates for some hepatic and lipid parameters, although estimates were attenuated after multivariable adjustment and were characterized by considerable uncertainty. CONCLUSIONS: ADV was detected in serum from individuals without occupational exposure living outside the immediate vicinity of the manufacturing source. ADV-N2 was the most frequently detected isomer and showed sex-related differences and different age-related patterns in women and men. These findings expand the available evidence on human exposure to ADV beyond occupational settings and support further investigation of its environmental distribution, exposure determinants, and potential health effects.

title: Mercury exposure during pregnancy and the effect of harmonised fish-consumption advice: results from the multi-country randomised HBM4EU-MOM study
abstract: Mercury exposure during pregnancy remains a public health concern due to its potential impact on foetal neurodevelopment. The randomised HBM4EU-MOM study (2020-2022) evaluated the effect of harmonised dietary advice on mercury exposure among 654 pregnant women from five European coastal countries. Total mercury concentrations in hair were measured at Phase 1 (baseline) and Phase 2 (follow-up). At baseline, mercury exposure varied substantially across countries, with the highest geometric mean (GM) concentrations in Portugal (1.56 μg/g) and Spain (0.90 μg/g), and lower levels in Greece, Iceland, and Cyprus (0.44 μg/g, 0.36 μg/g, and 0.31 μg/g, respectively). The primary adjusted analysis (n = 600) showed no evidence that the dietary intervention reduced follow-up hair mercury concentrations compared with the control group (adjusted geometric mean ratio [GMR] = 1.028, 95% CI 0.955-1.107; p = 0.455). Between baseline and follow-up, the GM mercury concentration across pooled participants with paired measurements decreased from 0.59 μg/g to 0.55 μg/g (-6.79%, p = 0.002), with statistically significant temporal reductions observed in Spain and Portugal, while no statistically significant temporal changes were observed in Greece, Iceland, or Cyprus. The proportion of women exceeding the EFSA exposure benchmark (1.8 μg/g) decreased from 12.5% at baseline to 7.5% at follow-up. Country-specific temporal reductions in Spain and Portugal were observed in both intervention and control groups with similar magnitudes. These findings indicate that the observed temporal decline in mercury exposure during pregnancy cannot be attributed specifically to the harmonised dietary intervention and is likely to reflect factors operating beyond the intervention itself. Although the intervention did not produce a measurable reduction in mercury exposure compared with standard care, the country-specific temporal patterns and reductions in the proportion of women exceeding health-based exposure benchmark highlight the importance of understanding the behavioural, dietary, and contextual factors influencing mercury exposure during pregnancy.

title: Strategy for mixture risk assessment using European human biomonitoring data: lessons learned from applications to pesticides, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and metal(loid)s
abstract: Humans are exposed daily to mixtures of chemicals from multiple sources and routes, including diet and the environment. These combined exposures may cause adverse health effects that are not adequately captured by conventional substance-by-substance risk assessment, due to the inherent complexity of assessing combined risks. To address this gap, the Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC) Real-life Mixtures project aims to consolidate scientific knowledge regarding mixture risk assessment (MRA). In synergy with ongoing activities of European agencies and other initiatives, this project developed a strategy to perform MRA using human biomonitoring (HBM) data. The approach consists of five steps: (1) prioritisation of chemical mixtures of interest for human health to guide case-study selection; (2) collection and organisation of the data required for MRA, including exposure, hazard, and toxicokinetic information; (3) development of methods for conducting MRA using HBM data; (4) implementation of these methods within the Monte Carlo Risk Assessment (MCRA) toolbox; and (5) application of the strategy to prioritised case studies. Three chemical families and four associated adverse health outcomes were selected based on the results of PARC priority process: pesticides affecting the nervous system, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) affecting the immune system, and metal(loid)s affecting kidney function and neurodevelopment. HBM data from studies conducted across Europe and Greenland were harmonised using the HBM data toolkit. Hazard and toxicokinetic data were compiled to derive internal toxicological values suitable for MRA. The MRA was then performed in a harmonised way for each case study using the MCRA toolbox. The strategy developed within the PARC Real-life Mixtures project provides a proof-of-concept for conducting HBM-based MRA and for informing policymakers. Future research will focus on reducing uncertainties and expanding the approach to additional chemicals with common health endpoints and co-exposure.

title: Passerine birds as bio-indicators of pesticide levels in farmlands and gardens: mitigation by organic farming and distance from treated fields
abstract: Both farmworkers and residents living near agricultural areas face adverse health outcomes prevailingly attributed to pesticides. Proximity to intensive agricultural areas may increase exposure, although this association remains debated, partly because collecting human biological samples is difficult. Therefore, identifying relevant bioindicators of environmental pesticide exposure could provide an alternative approach, and passerine birds are promising candidates given their close coexistence with humans. Here, we compared pesticide levels and profiles in passerines from farmland hedgerows and residents' gardens within the same rural area, and explored the effects of two mitigating components, assuming lower pesticide pressure with a higher percentage of organic farming (%OF) around hedgerows and with greater distance from the nearest treated crop for gardens. Blood samples were collected from 217 individuals across 11 species, and 111 pesticide residues were analysed. Contamination levels and profiles did not differ between farmlands and gardens, suggesting pervasive pesticide occurrence driven by environmental persistence and broad-scale dispersal. In farmland, model-estimated pesticide concentrations declined by 61.3 % (95 % CI: 32.5-77.8 %) as %OF increased from 0 to 100 %. In gardens, the model-estimated number of compounds and pesticide concentrations decreased with distance to the nearest conventional plot by 30.1 % (95 % CI: 6.8-47.6) and 70.1 % (95 % CI: 49.2-82.4), respectively. These effects were species-dependent, suggesting that certain species, such as the European robin, are more relevant indicators of local pesticide levels, likely due to their smaller home ranges. By showing that bird contamination reflects local agricultural practices and proximity, this study supports using passerines as effective sentinels of local environmental pesticide pressure, offering a valuable proxy for assessing ecological exposure in environments shared with human populations.

title: Equivalence testing in pesticide risk assessment: evaluation and practical guidance for design, analysis and interpretation
abstract: Harmful pesticide effects exceeding specific protection goals (SPG) may go undetected in underpowered studies. Regulatory honeybee field studies have consistently failed to reach the statistical power required under European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) guidance, which may have contributed to the approval of high-risk substances. Therefore, EFSA advised a shift from testing the null hypothesis of 'no effect' (difference testing) to equivalence testing. Under this new approach, a pesticide is classified as 'low risk' if the null hypothesis that its effect exceeds the SPG can be rejected. For honeybees, the recommended SPG is a colony size reduction below 10%. Critics have argued that this framework requires excessive experimental effort to demonstrate pesticide safety and proposed an alternative equivalence test defining treatment effects relative to the lower bound of the 90%-control-group confidence interval. Using simulations mimicking a regulatory honeybee field study, we show that although the two equivalence tests share the same trade-off between false 'low-risk' and false 'high-risk' classifications, only EFSA's equivalence test reliably identifies pesticides with effects > SPG at α = 0.2. Our results show that increasing sample sizes beyond current practice is often necessary for reliable regulatory assessment. However, for pesticides with effect sizes ≤ 5%, sample size requirements remain lower than those implied by the power requirement of EFSA's former difference-test-based guidance. Moreover, covariate adjustment - through a model term or balanced colony allocation using anticlustering randomisation - can reduce sample size requirements without losing power and thus save costs. Finally, we provide practical guidance for anticlustering randomisation, equivalence testing and their implementation in R.

title: Corrigendum to “Two decades of spatial and temporal pesticide risk to non-target invertebrates in England farmlands” [Environ. Int. 204 (2025) 109856]
Characterization of metal exposure from electronic cigarette use in Maryland, USA, via urine biomarkers
abstract: Electronic cigarette (e-cigarette) use has grown rapidly, although exposure from metals remains unclear. We investigated how e-cigarette use is associated with urinary metals. Study participants recruited from 2015 to 2020 (n = 209) were adults from Maryland who exclusively used e-cigarettes (n = 135) or used no tobacco products (n = 74). We measured concentrations of 6 toxic metals (via ICP-MS) and the nicotine metabolite cotinine (via ELISA) in participants’ urine samples. We also measured metals in aerosol from participants’ e-cigarettes. We compared urinary metal concentrations between use groups (e-cigarette use vs. non-use) using geometric mean regression. Within the e-cigarette use group, we also compared metal concentrations across tertiles of (i) urinary cotinine and (ii) corresponding aerosol metal concentrations. E-cigarette use was associated with 84 % higher urinary chromium and 61 % higher urinary lead. E-cigarette use in the highest cotinine tertile was associated with 93 % higher urine cadmium and 91 % higher urine chromium compared to the lowest tertile. The highest aerosol nickel tertile was associated with 66 % higher urinary nickel than the lowest tertile. Our findings suggest e-cigarette use and frequency may be associated with increased exposure to toxic metals. These findings support the need for regulation to consider implementing limits to metal content and subsequent exposure.

title: Prenatal phthalate exposure and early childhood asthma: a prospective birth cohort study from the Japan Environment and Children’s study
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prenatal phthalate exposure has been associated with allergic outcomes; however, evidence linking it to childhood asthma remains inconsistent. Using data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS), we examined the association between prenatal phthalate exposure measured during the first and second/third trimesters and current asthma in early childhood. METHODS: Among 9,707 mother-child pairs with urinary phthalate measurements in both the first and second/third trimesters, 8,554, 8,048, and 7,722 singleton children with available asthma data were analyzed at ages 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. Current asthma was defined as wheezing in the past 12 months together with caregiver-reported physician-diagnosed asthma during that period (or ongoing asthma treatment). In the primary analyses, first-trimester, second/third-trimester, and average concentrations were analyzed using logistic regression adjusted for maternal allergy or asthma history, smoking, education, household income, parity, and recruitment center, with multiple imputation and false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional analyses included sex stratification, generalized estimating equations, mutually adjusted trimester-specific models, alternative asthma definitions, and quantile g-computation. RESULTS: Current asthma prevalence was 6.4, 5.8, and 4.4% at 2, 4, and 6 years, respectively. In the primary analyses, no associations remained statistically significant after FDR correction. Similarly, generalized estimating equation and quantile g-computation analyses showed no significant overall associations after FDR correction. In additional analyses after FDR correction, the average monomethyl phthalate (MMP) concentration was positively associated with International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC)-defined asthma at age 2, while first-trimester and average MMP concentrations were positively associated with later-confirmed age-2 asthma. These findings were not consistently observed across ages or analytic approaches. CONCLUSION: Prenatal phthalate exposure was not consistently associated with current asthma in early childhood in this large Japanese birth cohort. Although certain MMP associations emerged in secondary and sensitivity analyses, the overall pattern of findings did not support a robust association.

title: Dose- and duration-dependent hepatotoxicity of PFO4DA: Divergent PPARα responses and conserved glucocorticoid receptor suppression
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) alternatives, such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl ether carboxylic acids (PFECA), have been widely detected in environmental and biological samples; however, their hepatic toxicity mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study focused on a representative PFECA compound, perfluoro-3,5,7,9-tetraoxadecanoic acid (PFO4DA), and investigated its hepatotoxic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms by integrating multi-omics analyses with in vitro assays. The results demonstrated that PFO4DA is a weak peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) agonist and exhibits dose-dependent regulation of PPARα signaling in vivo. Specifically, subacute high-dose exposure (0.4, 2, and 10 mg/kg/day for 28 days) activated PPARα signaling, whereas chronic low-dose environmentally relevant exposure (2 and 10 μg/kg/day for 140 days) indirectly suppressed PPARα activity, likely due to reduced availability of endogenous ligands. Metabolomic and lipidomic analyses revealed that chronic low-dose PFO4DA exposure induced broad depletion of multiple lipid species, particularly free fatty acids (FFAs) and their derivatives, thereby substantially reshaping hepatic metabolic homeostasis. Regardless of exposure scenario, glucocorticoid receptor (GR) signaling was consistently suppressed, suggesting that GR inhibition is a conserved toxicological feature of PFECA exposure. Moreover, amino acid profiles were broadly disturbed, accompanied by dysregulation of nutrient-sensing regulators, including ATF4 and FGF21. These findings extend the current understanding of PFECA-induced hepatotoxicity beyond classical nuclear receptor pathways and highlight the critical involvement of nutrient-sensing and metabolic regulatory networks. Collectively, this work identifies exposure-dependent divergence in PPARα signaling but conserved GR suppression as central features of PFO4DA hepatotoxicity, providing mechanistic insight essential for environmental health risk assessment of emerging PFAS alternatives.

title: Indoor NO2, temperature, and humidity in relation to maternal stress, sleep, and cognitive performance during pregnancy
abstract: Background Evidence characterising indoor environmental exposures and their effects on maternal neurobehavioural well-being during pregnancy remains scarce. Aim To estimate the associations between indoor residential environmental exposures (nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ), temperature, and relative humidity (RH)) and maternal neurobehavioural well-being (measured as perceived stress, sleep quality, and cognitive performance). Methods We included pregnant individuals (n = 906) from the population-based Barcelona Life Study Cohort (BiSC) who were recruited from 2018 to 2021. Weekly average indoor residential NO 2 concentrations, temperature, and RH were objectively measured in participants’ homes at ∼ 12 and ∼ 32 weeks of gestation using indoor monitoring devices. Linear, negative binomial, and mixed-effects regression models estimated the associations between indoor environmental exposures and perceived stress (10-item Perceived Stress Scale [PSS-10]), sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index [PSQI]), and cognitive performance (N-back reaction time and Primary Mental Abilities-Revised [PMA-R]); PSQI was assessed at both visits, while PSS-10 and cognitive tests were performed at ∼ 32 weeks of gestation only. Results After covariate adjustment, higher indoor NO 2 exposure was associated with higher perceived stress (0.66 points (95 % confidence interval [CI] 0.11, 1.21; p = 0.019)) and a greater increase in PSS-10 scores for a NO 2 interquartile range increase (11.2 µg/m 3 ) but not with sleep quality or cognitive performance. Indoor temperature and RH metrics, including nighttime minima and maxima, were not associated with any outcome. Conclusion Our findings suggest an association between indoor NO 2 concentration and prenatal perceived stress, indicating that the residential environment may be a relevant factor in maternal antenatal health that warrants further investigation.

title: Tiered human health risk assessment of colorants of emerging regulatory concern in household products
abstract: Colorants in household products may contribute to direct human exposure, yet occurrence, migration, and health-risk data remain limited. We investigated 205 visibly colored products, including kitchen cleaning products, disposable wiping products, and disposable food-contact articles, for 40 target colorants using LC–MS/MS and applied a tiered assessment to characterize human health risks and identify chemical–product combinations of potential concern. Ten colorants were detected. Paper napkins showed the greatest diversity, with at least one target detected in 10 of 23 samples. Basic Violet 10 was detected in 8 of 23 napkins at a median of 2.45 mg/kg (range, 0.154–1,147 mg/kg). In food-contact articles, Basic Violet 10 and Solvent Yellow 114 migrated at 8.55 and 793 μg/L, respectively. Tier 1 screening identified potential concern for Basic Violet 10 (cancer MOE, 475) and Basic Violet 3 (non-cancer MOE, 3,069). Tier 2 refined these compounds and additionally evaluated Solvent Yellow 14 and Pigment Red 53, which were prioritized based on carcinogenicity- or genotoxicity-related hazard evidence despite no Tier 1 screening concern. Follow-up napkin migration testing detected measurable migration only for Basic Violet 10. Its P95 non-cancer and cancer MOEs were 5.78 × 10 3 –1.15 × 10 4 and 1.97 × 10 4 –3.91 × 104, respectively, above their target MOEs, although the cancer margins were comparatively narrow. For paper straws, the combined beverage-migration and lip-contact scenario yielded P95 non-cancer and cancer MOEs of 1.55 × 10 5 –1.65 × 10 6 and 5.26 × 10 5 –5.60 × 10 6 , respectively. Sensitivity analysis identified pathway-specific exposure drivers, with napkin exposure dominated by use frequency and migration level and straw exposure driven by beverage intake for migration-related ingestion and use frequency for lip-contact transfer. Overall, appreciable health concern was not identified under the evaluated scenarios, although the comparatively narrow cancer MOE for Basic Violet 10 in paper napkins warrants cautious interpretation and may merit continued monitoring.

title: Long-term ambient heat and overall mortality among California participants in the Multiethnic Cohort study
abstract: Background and objectives Most heat-mortality studies have investigated short-term exposures, and few studies have examined the impacts of long-term heat exposure on mortality, on an individual level. We investigated prospectively the associations of long-term average daily maximum temperature (TMMX) at residential locations, and heat waves, averaged annually for up to 25 years, with overall and cause-specific mortality. Methods 88,283 California participants of the Multiethnic Cohort Study (∼70 % African American and Latinos) were followed for mortality from 1993 to 1996 (baseline) through 2019. Using Cox proportional hazards models we estimated hazard ratios (HR) and 95 % confidence intervals (CI) per 5°F (interquartile range) increase in time-varying TMMX adjusting for individual- and neighborhood-level, and other heat-related and adaptation factors. We investigated the modifying effects of PM 2.5 and O 3 and conducted various subgroup analyses. Results Overall mortality (n = 48,272 deaths) increased 5 % (HR 1.05, CI 1.03–1.08) per 5°F increase in TMMX. This statistically significant association remained when further adjusted for other climate factors. Cumulative heatwave exposures at the 75th and 90th percentile TMMX thresholds were also associated with mortality. Although formal tests for heterogeneity were not statistically significant for age, sex, race/ethnicity, neighborhood socioeconomic status (nSES), or climate zone, statistically significant associations were observed among those aged ≥ 85 (HR 1.06, CI 1.02–1.10), African American participants (HR 1.06, CI 1.01–1.11), and those living in inland climate zones (HR > 1.05). Participants in the highest tertiles of PM 2.5 and O 3 showed an HR of 1.52 (CI 1.30–1.78) per 5°F TMMX compared to 1.06 (CI 0.97–1.15) for those in the lowest tertiles of PM 2.5 and O 3 . TMMX was associated with increased mortality due to Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia and heart diseases. Conclusion Our findings of increased risk of all-cause and cause-specific mortality with increasing long-term average TMMX in a racially, ethnically, and socioeconomically diverse cohort provides timely evidence that sustained ambient heat as a chronic driver of mortality as well as an acute hazard. This evidence helps to inform future climate health research and intervention development.

title: Breastfeeding duration and residential setting in relation to childhood exposure to organochlorine pesticides and PCBs: a longitudinal study of the Rhea cohort in Crete
abstract: Despite decades-old bans, persistent organic pollutants (POPs), including organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), remain a public health concern owing to persistence and bioaccumulation. Previous Rhea mother-child cohort analyses (Crete, Greece) reported notably high DDE (DDT's main metabolite) in children, raising questions about postnatal pathways sustaining this post-ban burden. We aimed to characterise associations of residential setting, breastfeeding duration and childhood diet with children's serum OCP and PCB concentrations, accounting for maternal prenatal serum concentrations. Using linear mixed-effects models, we related breastfeeding duration and residential setting to 947 serum measurements from 443 Rhea children at ages 4, 6.5 and 11 years (n = 375, 239 and 333, respectively). Breastfeeding duration showed the strongest associations, with >4 months (versus never) consistently associated with higher DDE+DDT sum, HCB and PCB concentrations. Associations were strongest at age 4, then attenuated, consistent with growth dilution and elimination, but remained statistically detectable for DDE+DDT sum to age 11, independent of recent diet and parental agricultural occupation. Breastfeeding duration associations were stronger at higher maternal prenatal HCB concentrations (borderline for PCBs), consistent with lactation as one route of maternal-to-child transfer of accumulated body burden. Contrary to the hypothesis that agricultural proximity drives exposure, urban versus rural Heraklion residence was not significantly associated with serum POPs after adjustment for maternal prenatal concentrations, diet and household characteristics. Rather than implying any change to breastfeeding practice, these findings support reducing POP body burden in reproductive-age women, particularly before conception, during pregnancy and lactation, through continued exposure monitoring.

title: Regulatory aspects of risks posed by veterinary medicinal products to European necrophagous birds: A case study with nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)
abstract: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are used in human and veterinary medicine to treat pain and inflammatory diseases. However, the uncontrolled treatment of free-roaming and sheltered livestock with NSAIDs, mainly diclofenac, has caused catastrophic impacts on the biodiversity of necrophagous birds. For instance, a decline of up to 95 % in populations of various species of vultures occurred in South Asia from the late 1990 s to the early 2000 s. In the European context, the European Commission mandated the European Medicines Agency (EMA) to assess the risk posed by diclofenac to necrophagous bird populations in 2014. The risk assessment conducted by the EMA in 2014 identified the risks to affected species. Specific risk-management measures were proposed to facilitate an acceptable level of protection for necrophagous bird populations. Over the last ten years, just one evident death of a necrophagous bird due to intoxication with diclofenac was recorded in Europe. However, the concentrations of different NSAID residues detected in bird carcasses and tissues indicate exposure of avifauna to this group of pharmaceuticals, suggesting that scavenging birds in Europe are not protected against NSAIDs and other veterinary medicines used in animals for human consumption. In addition, NSAIDs are widely used in human medicine and are commonly detected in surface waters of EU member states. We assessed the risk of secondary poisoning based on the detected concentrations of diclofenac in surface waters and identified a risk for piscivorous raptors. We conclude that obligatory risk assessment followed by risk-management measures during the authorisation process does not sufficiently reduce the risk of pharmaceuticals for necrophagous and piscivorous raptors. We propose recommendations and alternative risk-management strategies, underscoring the urgency of protecting European necrophagous and piscivorous raptor populations to sustain the crucial ecosystem services they provide.

title: Zearalenone acts as a molecular glue to promote K33-linked ubiquitination and degradation of PPARγ and Its effects on glucose metabolism are mitigated by C3G
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEA) is a prevalent food-borne mycotoxin associated with metabolic disorders, yet its direct protein targets and the underlying mechanisms of its glucotoxic effects remain largely elusive. Here, we identify peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) as a molecular target of ZEA and demonstrate that ZEA exposure induces a mismatch between PPARγ transcription and protein abundance by promoting its ubiquitination, revealing a novel mechanism underlying ZEA-induced disruption of glucose homeostasis. In vivo, mice exposed to low-dose ZEA (0.5 mg/kg·bw, 5 days) or chronic ZEA combined with a high-fat diet exhibited significant glucose metabolic impairment, which was effectively ameliorated by co-administration of cyanidin-3-O-glucoside. Mechanistically, using HepG2 cells and HEK293T cells co-transfected with hPPARγ and HA-tagged ubiquitin mutants, combined with co-immunoprecipitation, cellular thermal shift assay, drug affinity responsive target stability, microscale thermophoresis, glucose uptake assays, and immunofluorescence, we demonstrate that ZEA functions as a molecular glue, facilitating K33-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of PPARγ, thereby suppressing its transcriptional activity and downstream glycolytic gene expression. Notably, C3G competitively binds to PPARγ, preventing ZEA-induced ubiquitination and stabilizing PPARγ protein levels, which restores glucose metabolic function. Furthermore, ZEA-mediated PPARγ depletion partially blunts the therapeutic efficacy of rosiglitazone, a PPARγ agonist, whereas C3G supplementation rescues this effect. Collectively, our findings uncover an unprecedented molecular-glue mechanism for mycotoxin-induced metabolic toxicity and highlight C3G as a potential dietary antagonist that safeguards PPARγ stability and glucose homeostasis against ZEA insults.

title: Protective effect and mechanism of Streptococcus D19T fermentation supernatant in asthmatic mice exposed to PM2.5
abstract: Allergic asthma is a common chronic respiratory disease, and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤ 2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ) remains a major environmental risk factor contributing to its global burden. However, effective preventive and therapeutic strategies for asthmatic airway inflammation with PM 2.5 exposure remain limited. D19 T , a novel Streptococcus strain isolated from the oropharynx of healthy children, has a favourable safety profile; furthermore, its fermentation supernatant exhibits antibacterial and anti‑inflammatory activities. This study found that D19 T treatment reduced inflammatory markers and improved redox status in a mouse model of asthma with PM 2.5 exposure. Non‑invasive respiratory function analysis confirmed improved lung function. Furthermore, the results showed that D19 T treatment modulated the oropharyngeal and gut microbiota and systemic metabolic profiles. Overall, this study provides new evidence supporting cell‑free fermentate‑based interventions for asthmatic airway inflammation in cases of PM 2.5 exposure.

title: Immunotoxicity and hepatic transcriptomic responses in zebrafish co-exposed to LDPE microplastics and zinc sulfate
abstract: Microplastics and heavy metals are ubiquitous co-contaminants in aquatic environments, yet their combined immunotoxic effects remain poorly understood. This study investigated the individual and combined toxicities of LDPE microplastics and ZnSO 4 in zebrafish across multiple biological levels. LDPE-associated material accumulated mainly in the gastrointestinal tract and liver, with ZnSO 4 co-exposure possibly influencing hepatic retention. Co-exposure exacerbated developmental toxicity, reducing survival, body length, and hatching rate while increasing malformations. In larvae, LDPE induced concentration-dependent ROS bursts; in adults, chronic exposure reduced ROS, with co-exposure restoring control levels. Apoptosis and neutrophil dynamics showed time- and concentration-dependent biphasic patterns. Flow cytometry revealed persistent erythroid and myeloid expansions, lymphocyte depletion, and precursor cell alterations. Transcriptomic profiling showed that LDPE alone enriched the ubiquitin–proteasome pathway, whereas co-exposure was associated with a shift toward sphingolipid/retinol metabolism, C-type lectin receptor signaling, and ferroptosis, accompanied by persistent inflammatory signatures. These findings indicate that ZnSO 4 co-exposure is associated with a shift in the LDPE response from acute proteotoxic stress toward sustained immune modulation, which may affect host immune competence. This study provides novel insights into the immunotoxicological risks of combined microplastic–heavy metal pollution.

title: An AOP-anchored framework integrating omics-derived potency and PBK simulations to support mechanistic chemical risk assessment
abstract: Despite the increasing use of omics data in toxicology, quantitatively linking in vitro molecular responses to human‑relevant exposure remains a key challenge for the regulatory assessment of per‑ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). In this work, an AOP‑anchored framework is proposed to integrate transcriptomic dose–response modelling with ensemble physiologically based kinetic (PBK) simulations to translate in vitro molecular perturbations into exposure‑relevant, mechanistically interpretable metrics. By linking gene‑ and key event (KE)‑level responses to PBK‑predicted internal concentrations, our framework enables both forward contextualization of early molecular changes and reverse dosimetry‑based estimation of human‑equivalent doses within structured KE networks. This integration enables estimation of the probability that PBK-predicted internal concentrations exceed transcriptomics-derived KE-level points of departure (PODs) while accounting for uncertainty in both transcriptomic modelling and PBK simulations. Application to PFOS and PFOA liver spheroid data suggests distinct mechanistic profiles: PFOA showed a focused lipid‑centric response consistent with steatosis-related events, whereas PFOS induced a broader response involving lipid metabolism, xenobiotic receptor signaling, and stress pathways. KE‑level reverse dosimetry yielded human‑equivalent doses consistent with in vivo reference points, while free‑concentration analyses highlighted the role of bioavailability. Together, this exposure‑integrating workflow supports the translation of in vitro omics data into mechanistically interpretable, regulatory‑relevant evidence and the identification of biologically plausible mechanistic hypotheses within the AOP framework, providing a scalable foundation for mechanistic risk assessment as additional data and models become available.

title: Heterogeneous health-economic outcomes of kitchen air purifier interventions: A 338-city study in urban China
abstract: Cooking is a major contributor to indoor PM 2.5 exposure and health risks. Here we developed a dynamic dual-zone model to estimate the potential city-, age-, and sex-specific changes in exposure and associated health-economic impacts of kitchen air purifier interventions across 338 Chinese cities in 2023. We evaluated one baseline (S0) and four interventions (S1–S4), where purifiers operated during cooking with post-cooking extensions of 0, 0.5, 1, and 2 h, respectively. Under S0, mean exposure was 58.6 µg/m 3 (95 % UI: 32.3–123.6). The model estimated that the interventions could reduce exposure by 11.2–16.2 %, corresponding to an estimated reduction of 3.3–4.2 % in PM 2.5 -attributable deaths. Net benefits versus S0 were estimated to be 88.7, 75.6, 48.3, and − 3.5 billion CNY for S1–S4, respectively.
